sentences.text: Napaisaurus guangxiensis is the sole species of an iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur discovered in the Early Cretaceous Xinlong Formation of Guangxi, China.
This animal belongs to the class Ornithischia and is part of the parent group Styracosterna.
It holds the distinction of being the first basal iguanodontian dinosaur named from southern China.
The genus name merges the type locality, the Napai Basin, with the Greek word for lizard, while the species name references the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a right ilium and ischium and was discovered in 2020.
Ji and Zhang formally described Napaisaurus as a new genus and species in 2022 based on diagnostic characters in the fossil material.
Napaisaurus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
